title: The organ wall as a sensory surface
objective: Locate where extrinsic afferent endings sit in the gut wall and why depth matters.

steps.title: Endings at every depth
steps.body: Extrinsic [[DRG]] afferents don't just touch the organ surface — their endings spread through the wall at defined depths: in the **[[mucosa]]** near the lumen, woven through the **[[muscularis externa|muscle layers]]**, and around blood vessels. *Where* an ending sits shapes *what* it senses.

steps.prompt: Why does the wall-depth of an afferent ending matter?
options: Different depths are exposed to different stimuli (stretch vs luminal chemistry)
Deeper endings in the wall always conduct their signals faster than the shallow ones do
Mucosal endings sense stretch best because they sit nearest the contents
The ending's depth changes where its own cell body is located
steps.explanation: An ending in the muscle layers is positioned to feel stretch; one near the lumen is positioned to sample chemistry. Position = tuning. Depth doesn't change conduction speed or where the cell body (the DRG) lives.

variants.setup: Two afferent endings sit at different depths in the gut wall.
variants.prompt: What does that difference most affect?
options: Which stimuli each ending is exposed to
How fast each ending's axon conducts
Where each ending's cell body sits
variants.reveal: Depth sets which stimuli an ending meets — stretch in muscle, chemistry near the lumen.

steps.setup: An afferent ends as a net woven between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers.
steps.prompt: What is it best positioned to sense?
options: Stretch of the gut wall as it fills or contracts
The exact chemical makeup of the luminal contents
Bacterial products touching the epithelial surface
Nutrient levels sampled directly from the lumen
steps.reveal: An ending embedded in muscle is mechanically coupled to the wall, so it reports stretch and contraction — not luminal chemistry, which a mucosal ending samples.

variants.prompt: An ending between the two muscle layers mainly senses…
variants.explanation: Muscle-embedded endings are positioned for mechanics (stretch), not chemistry.

sources.note: DRG subtypes tile the distal colon by force threshold; endings in defined wall layers.

reviewNotes: Ending position → tuning; builds on D6 gut wall.
